diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Reuters reported on Monday, 18 Aban, citing a senior Iranian source, that the attacks on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban, by the US on Qeshm Island targeted radar systems used in air defense and maritime navigation, missile launch bases, and naval mine systems. According to statistics from international maritime organizations released last week, attacks on oil tankers in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz sharply increased in October and have continued at the highest rate since the start of the war.

The Criminal Court Two of Ardabil sentenced a defendant to three months and one day of imprisonment for the charge of "disobedience to government officers during duty." Due to the defendant's lack of prior criminal record, the sentence was converted to 540 hours of free public service at one of the elderly care centers in the city.

The official Iraqi news agency confirmed that the secret trip of Ali Faleh Al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, to Tehran on Friday, 15 Aban, was made to reduce tensions and prevent escalation of war in the region. Tasnim News Agency reported that after talks with Donald Trump and Tom Barrack, Ali Al-Zaydi met with Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Tehran. It was also reported that Faleh Fayadh and Hadi Al-Amiri accompanied the Prime Minister on this trip.

Kosar Eftekhari, an eye injury victim of the nationwide protests, said at the international meeting "Women, Freedom, and Security" that the cries of those who are living evidence of the Islamic Republic's crimes must be heard. She added that they were shot in the eyes to silence them, but they will not allow this to happen and will continue the struggle.

Anwar Gargash, diplomatic advisor to the UAE president, said at the Abu Dhabi Strategic Dialogue on November 9 that the Middle East may face a prolonged period of instability because reaching a comprehensive political agreement between the US and Iran to end a war lasting over eight months seems difficult. Gargash added that the UAE has opposed the US war against Iran from the beginning.
Amanollah Baloochi and Hafez Abdulrahim Koohi, two Sunni clerics, were sent on leave from Zahedan prison.

Teddy Riner, a five-time Olympic gold medalist, officially announced his entry into the 2027 French presidential election campaign in a video posted on the social network X. He has founded a new party called "The France We Want" and considers himself a worthy candidate. Riner criticized the current state of his country and expressed concern about the spread of fear, France's debt burden, and the decline of government authority.

An explosion at the HABAŞ steel factory in the Aliağa district of İzmir province, Turkey, around noon on Monday, 18 Aban, led to a large fire and a massive column of smoke. Initial reports suggest that an overhead crane may have broken and fallen into the furnace while pouring molten steel, causing the explosion. Three people were killed and 14 injured, with 10 trapped under debris, and rescue teams are trying to reach them.

The Canadian government approved a new package of economic sanctions against 38 entities and 24 individuals linked to ballistic missile industries, cyber activities, and financial networks supporting Russia's war in Ukraine. Mahsa Mortazavi, a reporter for Iran International, reports.

According to IRNA, Sarfirouzabad district in Kermanshah, with 249 villages and a population of about 32,000, faces extensive shortages in water, roads, electricity, telecommunications, education, and healthcare services. IRNA reported that about 60 villages experience water stress, and water for 47 villages is supplied by tankers. Additionally, a lack of schools and educational facilities has forced some students to travel long distances to continue their education.

A video shows the mother of Sajedeh Karimi mourning while holding her daughter's bullet-ridden clothes ten months after her death. Sajedeh Karimi, 17 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 near Astaneh Ashrafiyeh.

Dariush Barani Biranvand, mayor of Khorramabad, announced that about 500 to 600 worn-out taxis are active in this city and that renewing the public transportation fleet requires financial and credit resources.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, on Monday, 18 Aban, identified the IRGC as responsible for the recent cyberattack on refrigerators in chain stores in France and warned that this action would have consequences for Iran. Barrot accused the IRGC of involvement in the attack but did not provide further details about possible consequences. Meanwhile, the Paris prosecutor's office requested international arrest warrants for the commander of the offensive cyber unit "Shaheed Kaveh" affiliated with the IRGC and two of his deputies.

UN experts expressed concern about increasing judicial and security pressures on independent lawyers, restricting their access to clients and cases, and interfering with the independence of bar associations. They also criticized pressure on female lawyers due to mandatory hijab requirements and preventing independent lawyers from participating in some political cases. According to a report by Harana, at least 135 lawyers faced judicial and security actions between Shahrivar 1404 and Shahrivar 1405.

Esteghlal Club announced that Alireza Koushki, a player of Esteghlal football team, after surgery due to respiratory problems in Ahvaz, traveled by land to Gachsaran to spend some time with his family. This player will go to Tehran for further treatment and medical care. Esteghlal Club wished him a full recovery.

Shirin Ebadi, Nobel Peace Prize laureate, announced that she dedicated her 29th honorary doctorate, received from Domingo Faustino Sarmiento University in Buenos Aires, Argentina, to the mothers seeking justice who lost their children in Dey 1404. Ebadi wrote in a message that she dedicates this honor to the mothers seeking justice who lost their children in Dey 1404. She also called for the establishment of democracy in Iran during her speech at the university and stated that the Iranian people oppose the government's policies that expose the country to tension and war.

Tehran Prosecutor's Office announced a judicial case against a gynecologist due to a video about the birth of four babies from single mothers. The doctor faces the charge of "spreading falsehoods" and their social media page has been blocked.

Fatemeh Sepahri, a political prisoner in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, continues to be deprived of specialized medical care and transfer to medical centers outside the prison despite multiple physical problems. Her brother stated that Fatemeh Sepahri reported severe pain in her right hand and the prison doctor prescribed an MRI, but no action has been taken to perform it so far.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Islamic Republic's Parliament, wrote on the social network X on Monday, 18 Aban, that Israelis are trying day and night to involve the United States in an endless war with the Islamic Republic. Ghalibaf wrote: "A quagmire that no president, whether now or in the future, whether Republican or Democrat, can get out of."

In two work-related incidents in the cities of Bonab and Mashhad, two workers died. One of them died in a beam and block production factory in Bonab while working with a concrete press machine, and the other died due to a wall collapse during demolition operations in Mashhad.

Behnam Taleblu, senior director of the Iran program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said that Donald Trump, by keeping diplomacy open and maintaining the military option, is seeking the least costly way to confront the Islamic Republic. According to him, the mediation efforts of Qatar and other Arab countries may delay a US military attack for several weeks or months, but cannot alone prevent a conflict. Taleblu added that the Trump administration, simultaneously with negotiations, continues the policy of maximum pressure and economic siege of the Islamic Republic, and that diplomacy alone is not sufficient to achieve America's strategic goals.

Farzin Dabiri, a member of the Football Federation's board, was suspended from the board membership and football activities until further notice due to not standing during the national anthem at Hamid Alidousti's funeral ceremony. The judicial authorities of the Football Federation held a meeting on Monday and suspended Dabiri's membership until the next board meeting on 9 Dey. Additionally, all of Farzin Dabiri's football activities were banned until further notice.

The execution of a 21-year-old prisoner was carried out in Behshahr prison. The tenth branch of the Criminal Court One of Tehran province sentenced a defendant in the case of killing a police officer to death. Additionally, three prisoners sentenced to death in separate cases were released from execution with the consent of the victims' families.

On Monday, 18 Aban, retired telecommunications workers held protests in 10 cities demanding full implementation of regulation 89/24 and salary adjustments. Also, workers of the National Industrial Steel Group of Iran in Ahvaz protested unpaid overdue wages and marched after gathering at the factory.
An audio version of Titrawal with Niusha Sarami was released about the meeting between Trump and the Prime Minister of Qatar and the involvement of China, Russia, and Turkey to prevent war.

Reza Tayebnia, a lawyer, was sentenced to six months in prison by Branch 103 of the Criminal Court Two of Kohgiluyeh County. The sentence was issued on the charge of "propaganda against the regime." This news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said the US "Iron Gates" plan is designed to prevent the transfer of advanced weapons and dual-use technologies through land borders and the Caspian Sea. He added the plan could disrupt financing of proxy groups and reconstruction of the Islamic Republic's arms industries and seems to target military equipment transfers from Russia and China with neighboring countries' cooperation. Mahdavi-Azad emphasized the plan may go beyond sanctions and be a significant military step in US pressure on the Islamic Republic.

Majid Aflaki, head coach of Iran's national taekwondo team at the Paris 2024 Olympics, said that because he posted a protest story in Dey month, he was told not to come to the national team's training anymore. The Iranian national team, under his leadership, won one gold, two silver, and one bronze at the Paris Olympics. Aflaki also led the national team to Asian and World Cup championships and earned the title of best coach in Asia.
Iran International reported that an audio version of Cheshmandaz titled "Iron Gates" has been released, addressing the new US plan to suffocate the IRGC.

Najmeh Amini, a 23-year-old student sentenced to death, remains in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. An appeal has been filed against her death sentence, and the Supreme Court has not yet made a decision regarding it. She has also been sentenced to imprisonment in a separate case.

A video shows a citizen releasing two white balloons in memory of Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi, executed protesters. These two protesters were among 12 defendants in the "Alikhani Square" case in Isfahan who were sentenced to death.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said the large gap between Tehran's and Washington's demands has made reaching a diplomatic agreement difficult. He added that the Islamic Republic is neither certain of the war being averted nor hopeful for the success of negotiations. Rahimpour also said that the results of the US midterm elections and political developments in Israel may affect the timing and manner of military actions but do not mean weakening Washington's and Tel Aviv's positions.

Adel Ferdosipour reacted to criticism about not standing during the national anthem at Hamid Alidousti's funeral on Football 360, saying the accusations do not stick to him and he has always loved his country. He added that despite facing restrictions, he has tried to stay in Iran and attract talented youth. He called the criticisms unfair and emphasized that Iran is his red line.

Donald Trump, after talks with the Prime Minister of Qatar, said that Qatar prefers the Iran issue to be resolved peacefully, but the US is ready for military strikes if necessary. Trump added that Saudi Arabia also prefers a peaceful resolution to the conflict with the Islamic Republic. He also defended Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War, saying Hegseth has won two wars.

Alhurra network, quoting a source in the Iraqi Foreign Ministry, reported that the Islamic Republic has introduced Abdolreza Mesgariyan, commander of the Ramadan Base of the Quds Force, as its new ambassador in Baghdad. He is to replace Mohammad Kazem Al-Sadegh, but the start date of his mission is not yet clear. Mesgariyan is responsible for security coordination between Tehran, Baghdad, and Erbil and also coordinates with Iraqi armed groups close to Tehran.

Iran International reported that Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, head coach of Esteghlal, said on Football Bartar that Ramin Rezaeian's departure from the team was for financial reasons, but he did not agree with the departure and the club supported him.

Trump said he had a very good conversation with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Prime Minister of Qatar, during which many issues related to the Islamic Republic of Iran were discussed. He stated that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, and other countries prefer to maintain the current situation, meaning the largest naval blockade in history and the new "Iron Gate" operation will continue. Trump emphasized that everyone agreed Iran cannot have nuclear weapons and the United States is fully armed and ready to act if there are any changes in the Middle East.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that the Chinese are trying to hold a trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi Jinping, and Putin in China, with one of the main topics being Iran and the future of the Islamic Republic. He asked whether China will become a second Guadeloupe and whether the fate of the Islamic Republic will be decided at the table of the three major world powers, and whether China and Russia are willing to sacrifice the Islamic Republic in a bigger deal with the US.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that Anwar Gargash, diplomatic advisor to the President of the UAE, warned that there is no solution available for regional conflicts and the Middle East is likely heading towards a period of instability and unrest; the UAE is preparing itself for the worst-case scenario.

Trump said on Truth Social that he had a "very good" contact with the Prime Minister of Qatar about the Islamic Republic. He added that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Kuwait, and other countries prefer to maintain the "status quo" regarding Iran. Trump also said that the largest naval blockade in history will continue and a new Iron Gate operation will be carried out, with operations continuing both on land and at sea.

Trump said in a White House press conference that the Islamic Republic, in addition to killing many American citizens, has killed "at least 75,000 protesters." He added that if they have to act again, they are in full military readiness and prepared to take action. Trump also said the conflict with the Islamic Republic is "quickly coming to an end" and that Iran will never obtain nuclear weapons.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that competition for power within the Islamic Republic has intensified. He added that Mohsen Rezaei's influence is increasing while Qalibaf's power is decreasing. He also said that Mohsen Rezaei is trying to take control of the equations with the US, Russia, and China.

Jean-Noël Barrot, the French Foreign Minister, identified the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as responsible for cyberattacks on the cooling systems of hundreds of food stores in France and warned that the Islamic Republic would face consequences for this action. Simultaneously, the Paris prosecutor's office has launched an investigation into the possible role of the hacking group known as "Shahid Kaveh" in these attacks.

Mohsen Rezaee wrote on X that the Iran war has shattered the US government and told Washington that the time has come to surrender to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly presented. He urged Washington to stop its desperate gambling and cease producing fake news about imaginary negotiations.

France says the IRGC hacked supermarket refrigerators in the country. The French foreign minister summoned the ambassador of the Islamic Republic and said this attack will have consequences for Tehran.

Iraq's state news agency reported that the country will temporarily close the Mandali border crossing with Iran from Friday to complete technical requirements. The report did not provide further details. In recent weeks, several border crossings between Iran and Iraq have been temporarily closed.

Trump said Iran's production capability has been severely reduced, with about 85% of this capability lost. He suggested that the conflict with Iran may soon end and emphasized that the US is fully armed and ready to act. Trump also stated that Iran will never have nuclear weapons and that the US has established the largest military blockade in history.

Donald Trump, after meeting with the Prime Minister of Qatar, announced that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Kuwait, and other regional countries want to continue the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and the Iron Gate operation. Trump added that these countries agree on preventing the Islamic Republic from obtaining nuclear weapons and reported progress toward ending the war. He said the US remains ready for military action but currently considers it unlikely.

Trump defended US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth against impeachment efforts, praising his military operations against Iran and Venezuela. Trump wrote on Truth Social that army recruitment has reached its highest level in history and that there have been two victories in Venezuela and Iran. He also called Republican Congressman Thomas Massey, who is pushing for Hegseth's impeachment, a "total loser."

Prince Reza Pahlavi described the Islamic Republic as a combination of the totalitarian features of the Soviet Union, Hitler's fascism, and the racist apartheid system during a press conference in Krakow, Poland. He emphasized that the international community has so far not taken decisive action against the Islamic Republic.

Trump said in an interview with C-SPAN that the reason for his current approach toward Iran is dialogue with regional countries and their preference to continue this approach instead of another attack. He said this attack would be "almost five times larger than the first attack." Trump added that in talks with these countries, he found they prefer the issue to proceed in this way and said, "Therefore, I also prefer to proceed in this way."

Erfan Ghanei-Fard, a Middle East analyst, said Tehran is changing its influence model in Iraq from political management of proxy forces to operational and security focus. He added this appointment aims to rebuild the command of proxy networks, control Iraqi armed groups, and keep Iraq as the Islamic Republic's backyard against the US and Israel.

Economic consequences of the war have intensified the unemployment crisis in Iran, pushing some dismissed workers to daily wage labor and street work. According to initial estimates by the Ministry of Labor of the Islamic Republic, over one million jobs have been lost during the war and about two million people have become unemployed directly and indirectly. Rouzbeh Boulehri explains the possibility of this number of unemployed people using unemployment insurance.

Reza Arab, a political analyst, said Donald Trump has the opportunity to expand military operations against the Islamic Republic before the new Congress begins its work, without potential congressional restrictions. He also said Baghdad does not have full control over armed groups affiliated with the Islamic Republic, and the best scenario for Iraq is the removal of the Islamic Republic and the possibility of exercising national sovereignty over these groups.

UN human rights experts, referring to security and judicial actions against at least 135 lawyers in Iran over the past year, called for the immediate cessation of arrests and intimidation of independent lawyers.

Gholamreza Mesbahi-Moghadam, a member of the Expediency Discernment Council, said that the patience and endurance of the people against economic difficulties imposed by the enemy to exhaust citizens have led the people to choose the path of resistance. He added that the Iranian nation, aware of the enemy's plan, has chosen resistance. Mesbahi-Moghadam also said that despite the ethnic and religious diversity in Iran, people agree on the axis of Islam and Iran, and the leadership has emphasized that criticisms should be expressed as concern, not as protests.

The Wall Street Journal reported from informed sources that following a threat from the Islamic Republic, the United States removed its military aircraft from a British airbase for the second time. American officials are still examining the exact nature of the threat against the RAF Mildenhall airbase in Britain. It is not yet clear whether the threat was immediate or more general in nature.

China's Foreign Ministry announced that Beijing is in contact with relevant parties about the possibility of holding a summit of the leaders of the US, Russia, and China aimed at ending the war with the Islamic Republic. China emphasized that the continuation of the war benefits neither side nor the international community and stressed the necessity of ending the conflicts.

Rouhollah Motafakker Azad, a member of the Parliament's presidium, said if the enemy makes a new mistake, the war will have bigger surprises for them. He added that all options to defend the country remain on the table. Motafakker Azad also said the armed forces have become more successful and precise in each war.

The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company announced on Tuesday, 19 Aban, that the number of ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz has been continuously increasing. The company's CEO told Reuters that alternative routes for servicing customers have been explored in recent months, but no final decision has been made yet.

Political analyst Rouhollah Rahimpour said Donald Trump is maintaining the US leverage in negotiations by refusing to guarantee an end to the war. According to him, the continuation of the naval blockade, sanctions, and restrictions on oil exports has increased economic pressure on the Islamic Republic.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic government, said that the atmosphere is completely warlike and they are in the midst of war. She attributed economic pressures to war and a harsh economic siege. She added that the government's decisions are aimed at preserving livelihoods and moving towards lasting peace.

A video received by Iran International shows that the mother of Mohammad Javad Moghadassi spoke on November 9, the tenth month after her son's killing: "They killed my son and I also died. My son was at the beginning of his peak, they must pay." Mohammad Javad Moghadassi, 28 years old, was shot in Tehran on January 9 and died the next day in the hospital.

The mother of Mohammad Javad Moghadassi said on Monday, 18 Aban, that the government fears the people and holds street gatherings to prevent their presence. Mohammad Javad Moghadassi, 28 years old, was shot in Tehran on 19 Dey 1404 and died the next day in the hospital.

Ali Safaei, a former Iranian Premier League referee, and Mojtaba Shojaei, a League One referee, reported on the program "360" by Adel Ferdosipour about suspicious calls to change match results, death threats, and being removed from refereeing after opposing these requests. Safaei said that two seasons ago, a member of the referees committee asked him to favor the opponent of Tractor in a match, and the following season he received a similar call about the Aluminium Arak match with a northern team, which he reported to federation officials but they refused to change the referee.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, said that gas cuts in Tehran depend on consumption levels, and if consumption is very high, gas may be cut across the country. She added that in past winters there was a shortage of about 300 million cubic meters of gas, and attacks on gas refineries caused a loss of 230 million cubic meters. Mohajerani emphasized that everyone must save gas and that Tehran residents are no different from other parts of the country.

Saman Ghoddos, a player of the Iran national football team, announced that after 9 years in the national team, he is ending his international career. He played 71 international matches and scored three goals during this period. In his farewell message, Ghoddos thanked his teammates, coaches, and fans, and said that the honor of captaining the national team will always hold a special place in his heart.

Najmuddin Tabasi, a member of the Society of Seminary Teachers of Qom, stated in a letter that after reviewing the views of several jurists and seminary professors and evaluating the works and jurisprudential discussions of Mojtaba Khamenei, he has become confident in his "absolute jurisprudence and ijtihad." Tabasi wrote in this letter that Mojtaba Khamenei meets the "necessary conditions for religious leadership" and that following him is permissible. Since the start of the war on 9 Esfand 1404 [Gregorian: 2026-02-28], no new images or audio files of the third leader of the Islamic Republic have been released.

Mizan, the media outlet of the Islamic Republic Judiciary, announced that following the judiciary chief's emphasis on identifying and confronting organized groups such as those promoting unveiled behavior and nudity, the Tehran prosecutor's office has intervened and judicial action is underway. Several individuals who, according to this media, promoted unveiled behavior and immorality have been arrested on Iranshahr Street in Tehran. The Tehran prosecutor's office warned that it will confront any behavior promoting nudity and licentiousness.

A video shows the mother of Mohammad Javad Moghadassi restless at his grave while cutting his birthday cake on Monday, 18 Aban. Mohammad Javad Moghadassi, 28 years old, was shot in Tehran on 19 Dey 1404 and died the next day in the hospital.

The Football Federation of the Islamic Republic announced that the travel plan of the national football team to Iraq for friendly matches in the November FIFA window has changed. Instead of a direct flight to Basra, the national team will first fly to Abadan and then travel by land to Basra. The national team is scheduled to play against Palestine on Saturday, November 14 at 18:30 Tehran time and against Iraq on Tuesday, November 17 at 19:45 Tehran time.

According to a video received by Iran International, the mother of the late Reza Eskandarpour said at the birthday ceremony of the late Mohammad Javad Moghaddasi and at his grave: "How long will the crimes of the Islamic Republic continue? They killed our children and now they are being executed." Reza Eskandarpour, 37 years old, was killed in Tehran on 18 Dey 1404 [Gregorian: 2026-01-08].

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump is currently giving diplomacy a chance to possibly end the war with lower costs. He emphasized that despite the efforts of Qatar and Turkey, the option of war remains on Trump's table and the failure of diplomacy could lead to military conflict.

Amid ongoing speculation about negotiations between the Islamic Republic and the US, officials from both sides consider reaching an agreement in the near future out of reach. Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, said Washington is not on the verge of an agreement with Tehran. In Iran, the government spokesperson rejected the status of neither war nor peace, stating the country is in a state of war.

Students and parents from various cities in Iran, including Amol, Tehran, Karaj, Ardabil, and Kermanshah, have reported gas cuts in schools and heating devices being turned off, protesting this situation. Simultaneously, reports of household gas cuts in some cities and villages have also been received.

Mohammad Dadkan, former head of Iran's football federation, said in an interview that Islamic Republic officials did nothing for the country in 47 years and filled their own pockets. He added that they sent their children abroad and distracted people with the 'Death to America' slogan.

Canada's Foreign Ministry announced on Tuesday, 19 Aban, that it has reinstated sanctions against 11 Iranian entities. These entities were previously removed from the sanctions list in 2016 due to Iran's progress within the JCPOA framework. Companies related to nuclear fuel, oil, and banks have been placed back on the sanctions list.
A collapse at a construction project in Mashhad resulted in injuries to two workers. These two workers were transferred from the negative fourth floor of the building to outside.

The mother of the late Aynaz Rahimi Hajiabadi shared a video in which she read part of her daughter's diary, where she wrote about her dreams. Aynaz Rahimi Hajiabadi, a 13-year-old teenager, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Najafabad, Isfahan province.

Al Arabiya reported on Tuesday, 19 Aban that the Gulf countries agreed to establish an advanced headquarters for unified military command in Kuwait. These countries also agreed to allocate military forces to the forward command that is to be opened in Kuwait.
Mona Maleki, a prisoner held in Sanandaj prison, was transferred to a hospital due to poor physical condition caused by gallstones.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Donald Trump has intensified the economic siege of the Islamic Republic by relying on military superiority and control over the Strait of Hormuz, while simultaneously giving diplomacy a chance. He stated that the Islamic Republic, by ignoring the reality of the balance of power and continuing its confrontational policy with the US, transfers the cost of this approach to the Iranian people's livelihood. Kazemian also emphasized that the claim that the Iranian people have chosen resistance is not true, and citizens are forced to endure government policies under pressure and repression.

The Cultural and Social Deputy of the West Tehran Province Police Command reported the identification and judicial action against a beauty salon in Shahriar due to the publication of images contrary to Islamic norms on social media. The operator of the Instagram page of this business unit was summoned and charged.

The 26th Knesset of Israel begins with the swearing-in of 120 members in Jerusalem. The ceremony is held with the presence of Isaac Herzog, the President, and Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister. Consultations between Netanyahu's opposition parties and ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties about the political arrangement of the parliament and the formation of a new government continue.

The public relations of the IRGC Navy announced that two oil tankers, which according to this entity were traveling in an "unauthorized route" in the Strait of Hormuz, caught fire. According to a statement by the IRGC Navy published on Tuesday, 19 Aban, one of the vessels, a supertanker, exploded after hitting a "naval mine," and the second tanker, which according to this entity was "under the protection of US military fighters" and traveling on an "illegal route," caught fire. The IRGC Navy also stated that these two tankers were navigating the Strait of Hormuz with their navigation and identification systems turned off and after hitting what was described as the "fire wall of the Strait of Hormuz," were abandoned on the southern shores of the strait.

Iranian media reported on Tuesday, 19 Aban, the unveiling of a new missile city belonging to the Aerospace Force of the IRGC. Ali Abdollahi and Majid Mousavi attended the unveiling ceremony. Ali Abdollahi said if the enemy tries to do anything wrong, our response will go beyond the region.

The trial of three Iranian suspects accused of spying on Iran International journalists is being held today at Woolwich Court in London, and their verdict is to be announced. These three individuals are accused of gathering information for the Islamic Republic. Tajeddin Soroush, a journalist from Iran International, reports.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said the US is seeking to limit a large part of Tehran's economic exchange routes by expanding the maritime, air, and land blockade of the Islamic Republic. According to him, the Trump administration hopes to force the Islamic Republic to accept Washington's conditions by intensifying economic pressure without entering a short-term military war.
Tehran's prosecutor's office reported the arrest of several citizens on Iranshahr Street for what it called "promoting unveiled behavior and immorality."

Parviz Sarvari, the deputy chairman of Tehran City Council, said a "mosquito-like spirit" has prevailed in the country. He likened critics who publish videos and photos of garbage in Tehran's gutters to sitting on "wounds and filth" and said they present one piece of garbage as a symbol of Tehran's waste situation. He added that the extensive and managed efforts of Tehran Municipality should not be questioned by a few fabricated videos.

Ezzatollah Soleimani, one of the detainees of the December 1404 protests, was sentenced to seven years and eight months in prison by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. He was sentenced to three years and seven months for assembly and collusion against national security, three years and seven months for insulting sacred beliefs, and six months for propaganda against the regime.

On the tenth month after the large massacre by the Islamic Republic in Dey 1404, the mother of the missing Mohammadparsa Amini released a video of her son and his 40th-day memorial ceremony on social media. Mohammadparsa Amini, a 17-year-old teenager, was killed on Dey 18, 1404 in Karaj.

Ali Abbasi, advisor to the governor of Isfahan on disability affairs, stated that there is no reliable data on the implementation of legal quotas for housing and employment of people with disabilities in this province. He said that the lack of allocation of some credits, poor coordination and accountability of agencies, and insufficient participation of people with disabilities in decision-making have caused problems in the implementation of their legal rights. Also, despite the provision of a 10% housing quota and a 3% employment quota for people with disabilities, no statistics on the implementation of these quotas in Isfahan have been published.

Farzin Dabiri, a member of the Football Federation's board, was suspended from all football activities for refusing to stand during the national anthem at the farewell ceremony for Hamid Alidousti, a former national team player.

According to the Football Federation, the Iraqi government has canceled the direct flight permit for the Iranian national football team from Tehran to Basra. Therefore, the team will fly from Mehrabad Airport to Abadan and then travel by bus to Basra. This was reported in an interview with Raha Pourbakhsh from Iran International.
Siamak Sadeghi Chehrazi, a teachers' union activist and board member of the Khuzestan Teachers' Union, was released on bail from Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic, said in a video that Netanyahu recently said either the Islamic Republic must be destroyed or they will be. Abdollahi added that the Islamic Republic will definitely destroy Israel and that Israel and the US are defeated. He also said surprises will reveal themselves in the future war.

Fotbali website reported that Yaser Asani, the Albanian player of Esteghlal, attended the disciplinary committee session of the Football Federation online on Tuesday morning and explained about his altercation with Alireza Ildrom, the assistant referee of the Esteghlal vs Esteghlal Khuzestan match. Asani received a second yellow card and was sent off in the final minutes of the twelfth week of the Premier League match. Esteghlal club claims that Ildrom insulted Asani's family, causing the tension, and Asani's lawyer presented a video file related to the alleged insult.

Despite three weeks passing since the arrest of Omid Ahmadi Nejad, a resident of Ahvaz, there is still no information about his place of detention or condition. A source close to his family confirmed this news and stated that the lack of information about his fate has caused concern among his family and relatives.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing a plate of fried eggplant and said: "This is our lunch today. Death to Mojtaba."
A 14-year-old girl who was a victim of child marriage was killed by her husband in Arzuiyeh County. The suspect was arrested by the police.

The father of Parnian Dabiri addressed the Islamic Republic officials in the tenth month after the January 1404 massacre, saying Parnian was beside him and they could have killed him but they killed his daughter. He added that the officials could have ended the protests without bloodshed but their goal was to suppress the people by the harshest methods. Parnian Dabiri, a 16-year-old teenager, was killed on 19 Dey 1404 in Baharestan County, Tehran Province.

Majid Mousavi, commander of the Aerospace Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, stated in a video titled "Unveiling of the new missile city of the IRGC" that if necessary, the Islamic Republic will target all enemy capacities in the region and beyond. He said they are prepared to confront any threat in the region and beyond and will deter the enemy from any mistakes.

Vincent Kompany, Bayern Munich's coach, returned to the club's training ground on Tuesday after several weeks away due to illness and fainting during training. Kompany, who had been absent since October 23 due to physical problems, attended his office and met with his assistant and the club's sporting director. After fainting during training and being diagnosed with meningitis, he spent his recovery period at home, during which Aaron Danks led the team.

Ali Abbasi, the director general of forensic medicine in Mazandaran, announced that during the first six months of this year, 231 people died in traffic accidents in this province and 8,941 were injured. Abbasi also reported a 15% increase in the number of injured compared to the same period last year. The counties of Sari, Babol, and Amol had the highest death tolls.

Tehran Prosecutor's Office filed charges against Zohreh Amiri, a gynecologist, for posting a video about the increase in births from single mothers in Iran. The doctor claimed in the video that the number of single mothers in Iran is rising. After the video was published, the prosecutor's office filed charges against her and her Instagram page was blocked.

A released video shows the mother of Alireza Khodadadeh visiting her son's grave and talking to him in the tenth month after the government's massacre in Dey 1404. Alireza Khodadadeh, 19 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Najafabad.

US Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, in defense of the country's military operations, said these operations were legal and carried out under the order of Donald Trump. He rejected the accusation of targeting civilians and said the US would not apologize for confronting drug traffickers and destroying the capabilities of terrorist regimes.

Mehdi Mohammadi, a 26-year-old resident of Sabzevar, was arrested by security forces on 9 Aban and remains in indefinite detention in Sabzevar prison after 11 days. This report was published by HRANA news agency.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, said he was informed that the economic pressure campaign against the Islamic Republic has been so successful that there is no longer a need for a large-scale military operation. He added that economic pressure on Iran will become even more intense in the future.
The Israeli parliament began its work with the swearing-in of members; however, the status of the future Israeli government is still unclear and efforts to form the government continue.

Pete Hegseth, US Secretary of Defense, said the Trump administration did not initiate military conflict with Iran and the Islamic Republic started the war 47 years ago. He called the Islamic Republic a terrorist regime and emphasized US readiness to attack Iran again.

Images and reports from Tehran show young people setting up stalls on sidewalks, saying economic pressures and lack of job opportunities have driven them to this income method. Reports indicate municipal officers have clashed with street vendors in Tehran and Shiraz. Tasnim News Agency reported that a plan to collect book vendors in Enghelab Street, Tehran, started on 29 Mehr and a previous plan to identify and relocate these vendors had not reached its final stage.
